texts: Maintain four explicit verification and integration outcomes: FunctionMatch (local body diagnostic with explicit external context obligations), RegionMatch -> immutable matcher-minted VerifiedRegion (closed object/region proof), PlacementPlan (single derived preflight partition plan shared by check_t3_buildable, wc1.build, wc1.emit, batch_driver, wave4a, and m2_inventory), and IntegratedResult (actual assemble, link, and hardened wc1.compare receipt). Do not add a separate CandidateRegion runtime class or persistent proof/CU metadata DB in M2.

Retain the separation between FunctionMatch (local diagnostic), RegionMatch -> immutable VerifiedRegion (closed object/region proof), and BuildAPlacementPlan (preflight placement plan), and enforce actual assemble, link, provider-provenance, and hardened loader comparison receipts (per DEC-A03 rev 2 / DEC-B03 rev 2) as the sole Build A integration-acceptance boundary. Pipeline consumers (wc1.match, wc1.build, wc1.t3_audit, wc1.m2_inventory, wc1.overnight, wc1.wave4) distinguish these levels using typed results without owning proof logic.

Before landing Fix B3 or any future selective OMF extraction pilot (post-M2), share one tested strict OMF32 record/fixup codec (record bounds, nonzero checksums, preserved explicit FRAME encodings, persistent cross-record THREAD, format/linker-verified record-length bounds) across verification and admitted OMF transforms, while leaving permissive library-signature readers untouched and avoiding unnecessary omfpatch refactoring during M2.

Before landing post-M2 Fix B3 or any later selective OMF extraction pilot, share one strict OMF32 subset codec for the supported record and fixup types (validating record bounds, nonzero checksums, single MODEND, persistent cross-record THREAD state, explicit FRAME encodings, and linker-tested record-size limits rather than an assumed 64-fixup ceiling), removing duplicate transform serializers without rewriting unrelated permissive readers or scheduling this work ahead of M2 completion.

Replace RFC §2.2.5 alignment premises with E2 empirically measured compiler behavior: Watcom 10.0a function spacing is 16 bytes under -4r -ot, 4 bytes under -3r/-5r -ot (with PARA 16-byte _TEXT SEGDEF for tested -ot), and 1 byte under -os/-od; OW2 uses 16 bytes under -4r and -5r. Keep -4r as the single-file project default with additive E7 presets (DEC-B11), rank -5r as the first-tried candidate family for multi-function -ot TUs requiring 4-byte spacing without claiming it was the universal 1994 project flag, and keep EXP-2/Q-B06 (5r -d1+ -zp1 and 5r -od) as optional additive probes.

Replace RFC §2.2.5's incorrect "10.0a always aligns to 4B" premise with E2's empirically verified alignment matrix (Watcom 10.0a -4r -ot = 16B, -5r/-3r -ot = 4B, -os/-od = 1B, with _TEXT SEGDEF = PARA 16B in the measured modes; OW2 -4r/-5r = 16B). Keep -4r as the project default, treat -5r as a first-tried candidate search family for multi-function TUs requiring 4-byte spacing without claiming original historical flags, and run EXP-2 to measure -5r -d1+ -zp1 and -od -5r.

history.title: M2 priority boundary for infrastructure work
history.proposition: Until gate 1 passes, only infrastructure that directly unblocks not-done in-scope functions, or that closes a known verification soundness gap, is admitted to production. On main@a21772b this is: the E0 matcher (DEC-B02), the single planner (DEC-B03), B2 (DEC-B04), B1 (DEC-B05), joint TUs (DEC-B06) and T4 paired-state symmetry (DEC-B07). Fix B3, selective extraction, the full E6 Group/Integrated machinery, persistent provenance and CU databases are scheduled on a post-M2/M3 track.

history.title: M2 admission principle for infrastructure work
history.proposition: Until gate 1 passes, a production infrastructure change is admitted only if it removes an observed blocker of named not-done in-scope functions or closes a demonstrated verification or toolchain soundness defect; routine reconstruction work proceeds in parallel and is not serialized behind infrastructure stages. On main@17733f9 the admitted items are: the E0 matcher with strict raw admission (DEC-B02), the single placement planner with integration receipts (DEC-B03), the cross-object transfer rule (DEC-B04, DEC-B19), the B1 leading-byte base (DEC-B05), proof-gated joint TUs (DEC-B06), complete T4 paired-state symmetry (DEC-B18), measured comparator strengthening (DEC-B20) and the compiler-facing path guard (DEC-B22); a deterministic rename/migration helper is admitted when a reconstruction batch demonstrably needs it. Fix B3, selective extraction, E6 Group/Integrated machinery beyond a named witness, persistent provenance stores and CU databases are scheduled on a post-M2/M3 track unless a named not-done function requires them.

history.title: Production adoption of E0 matcher semantics
history.proposition: tools/wc1/match.py adopts E0 semantics (bidirectional normalized obligations, leading bytes, local-data pointer targets, mutually exclusive verdicts with UNSUPPORTED precedence, untruncated machine findings), reimplemented in tools/ with E0's 55 controls as production tests. It is admitted only if the full current T3 population returns MATCH under make verify.

history.title: Production adoption of E0 matcher semantics with strict raw admission
history.proposition: tools/wc1/match.py adopts E0 semantics (bidirectional normalized obligations, leading bytes, local-data pointer targets, mutually exclusive verdicts with UNSUPPORTED precedence, untruncated machine findings), reimplemented in tools/ with E0's 55 controls as production tests. Production admission additionally requires strict raw-OMF input checks (record bounds, checksum when nonzero, single MODEND, record-type allow-list, cross-record THREAD state, explicit FRAME preserved) with unsupported input reported as UNSUPPORTED, and the proof is bound to the raw bytes of the exact object later consumed by the build. Local data, including CONST pad bytes, is matched exactly at cutover. A verdict may change from non-MATCH to MATCH only through a new, independently tested proof rule with positive and negative controls, never by relaxing an existing check; function-scoped diagnostic closure may record explicit external edge obligations but never grants placement. The cutover is admitted only if the full current T3 population returns MATCH under make verify.

history.title: Buildability predicate equals the integrator
history.proposition: wc1.build exposes one planner, plan(p, regions), that computes cuts, entries, cross-object branch emission modes and data anchors, plus errors. check_t3_buildable, batch_driver, wave4a and the m2 inventory call that planner, and the emitter consumes its output. A function may be reported "buildable" only if the planner returns no error and the emitter accepts the plan. Regression tests: IntroOpSyncSound standalone is rejected; Group B is accepted.

history.title: One planner; promotion requires an integration receipt
history.proposition: wc1.build exposes one planner, plan(p, regions), that computes cuts, entries, cross-object transfer encodings, adjacency obligations and data anchors, plus errors; check_t3_buildable, batch_driver, wave4a, m2_inventory and the emitter all consume that planner. A clean plan is a preflight result only: a function is promoted (src wiring for T3) only with an integration receipt recording the actual assembly, link and comparison (including the checks added by DEC-B20) of the exact plan. Regression tests are mode-qualified: standalone IntroOpSyncSound is rejected when the cross-object transfer rule is disabled or any spanned object is legacy-placed, accepted with recorded Build A debt when the rule is enabled in place, and Group B is accepted with no debt.

history.title: Full paired-state symmetry for all T4 runs
history.proposition: wc1.cemu.run_pair snapshots every mapped emulator memory region before the original execution and restores it before the C execution, so both executions start from identical complete state. The audit log records the restored set. The rule applies to all T4 tests (single- and multi-function). After adoption, each xfailed divergence test is re-run and reclassified by evidence. Changes to existing tests' expected status (XPASS → pass, removal of xfail) require owner approval.

history.title: Complete paired starting state for all T4 runs
history.proposition: Each T4 pair runs both sides from an equivalent complete starting state: CPU context (general registers, EFLAGS, segment registers and ESP), the full set of mapped memory regions and their contents (covering host and guest writes), emulator allocator state, and declared mutable stub state. Stubs keep mutable state in emulator memory or declare a per-run reset; otherwise the case reports UNSUPPORTED. State restoration is separate from the effects each test compares, and the audit log records the restored state. The rule applies to all T4 tests. Before landing, the full T4 suite runs once with the rule enabled; any change in an existing test's outcome or xfail status is presented to the owner. Reclassification of a divergence follows only from the test result after the change.

history.title: Plan-level exclusion of legacy-placed objects from fixed-displacement spans
history.proposition: The placement planner rejects any fixed-displacement cross-object branch whose source-to-target span includes an object placed in legacy layout. That covers both the global --legacy flag and the automatic per-object Unplaceable fallback.

history.title: CONST pad bytes are environment-dependent proof-irrelevant bytes
history.proposition: Watcom 10.0a CONST inter-literal pad bytes are treated as environment-dependent. They are excluded from proof-cache digests (normalized), never required to equal the original in any future V4 rule, and V4 (when adopted) is applied identically by the matcher and build.place(), with ASM as physical provider in Build A. Until V4 is adopted, objects with such pads fail closed.

history.title: CONST pad bytes are environment-dependent and exempt only on independent access proof
history.proposition: Watcom 10.0a CONST inter-literal pad bytes are environment-dependent (they vary with compile-input paths and are stable for fixed inputs in our probes) and are excluded from proof-cache digests by normalization. No exemption from exact data matching is granted on the basis of literal shape or the absence of relocation targets; any future exclusion requires independent extent, ownership and access evidence covering computed reads, is applied identically by the matcher and build.place(), and keeps ASM as the Build A physical provider. Until then such objects fail closed and the extern-literal idiom remains available.

history.title: Adopt Strict 5-Condition Watcom 10.0a `CONST` Uninitialized Alignment-Gap Rule (Invariant V4)
history.proposition: In both E0 `RegionMatch` and Stage-3 Fix B3, explicitly exempt 1..3-byte alignment padding gaps in `CONST` **if and only if** all 5 conditions hold: (1) segment is `CONST` (never `_DATA`/`_BSS`/`_TEXT`), (2) `1 <= len(gap) <= 3` ending at `align4(gap.start)`, (3) immediately preceded by `0x00` terminating a byte-identical verified literal, (4) zero object fixups and zero `war.exe` fixups/references target any byte in `gap`, and (5) `VerifiedRegion` records `const_pad_exempted = True` and forces `physical_provider = ASM` in Build A.

gpt.reason: The five conditions do not rule out computed or overlapping access and unnecessarily gate E0.
Literal shape plus a direct-reference scan cannot exclude a computed read.
Withdrawn. A computed read defeats gap predicates.

claude.reason: The pad premise is real (0x56b1c residue confirmed; compiled pad is environment-dependent). The 5-condition rule is reasonable. It is not M2-critical, because the extern-literal idiom exists in production (save_slot_path.c).
claude.conditions: (1) Re-describe as environment-dependent, not consecutive-run non-deterministic, unless fixed-input runs differ. (2) Apply the same rule in build.place() as in the matcher. (3) Digest normalization for caches. (4) Schedule on the first need (natural literals or B3), not Stage 0.
